Fares usually cover only a small part of running costs.
Free transport pays for itself through higher passenger numbers.
questions.explanation: Many new passengers 'previously walked or cycled, while fewer gave up their cars'. Fares often pay for a large part of running costs, and the cost of free transport must be covered from other public funds.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the passage?
questions.correct: Most cities have banned short-term rentals of whole flats.
wrong: Some cities limit how many nights a whole flat can be rented out.
Some platforms remove listings without a valid registration number.
questions.explanation: The passage says some cities limit the number of nights, not that most cities ban such rentals. The other three are all stated: limits on nights, many unregistered listings, and agreements under which platforms remove listings without a valid number.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Mixed-fibre fabrics are hard to turn into new ones.
wrong: Most collected textiles are in good enough condition to sell again.
Separate collection of textiles has solved the waste problem.
Recycling capacity for textiles is already more than enough.
questions.explanation: The technology to turn old fabrics, 'especially mixed fibres', into new ones is still limited. Much of what is collected is too worn for reuse, collection is 'only the first step', and critics call for more recycling capacity.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Most vertical farms grow fast-growing, high-value crops.
wrong: Vertical farms mainly grow wheat and other staple crops.
Vertical farms use more water than open fields.
Lighting is a minor part of a vertical farm's costs.
questions.explanation: Most vertical farms grow 'fast-growing, high-value crops such as salad leaves and herbs rather than staple crops such as wheat'. They use far less water than open fields, and lighting and climate control make up a large share of their costs.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
questions.correct: Assemblies can reflect the public, but their advice is not binding.
wrong: Citizens' assemblies make binding decisions for governments.
Members of citizens' assemblies are chosen by election.
Governments usually adopt all of an assembly's recommendations.
questions.explanation: Supporters say random selection gives a group that reflects the wider population; critics point out that the recommendations are not binding and that governments have sometimes adopted only a small number of them. Members are chosen at random, not elected, and nothing in the passage says that governments usually adopt every recommendation.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Most services offer remote and in-person consultations.
wrong: Remote consultations have replaced appointments in person.
Every condition can be assessed by video.
Older patients find remote consultations easier to use.
questions.explanation: Most services offer remote consultations 'alongside, not instead of' appointments in person. Some conditions need a physical examination, and older patients may find remote consultations harder to use.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Grazing can reduce fire risk on slopes that machines cannot reach.
wrong: Grazing is enough to prevent large fires in extreme weather.
Clearing land by machine is cheaper than grazing.
Experts see grazing as a replacement for firebreaks.
questions.explanation: Grazing reduces fuel and 'can reach steep slopes where machines cannot work'. It cannot prevent large fires in extreme weather on its own, it is cheaper than machine clearing, and experts see it as one tool alongside firebreaks.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the passage?
questions.correct: Rail has already overtaken road for most freight.
wrong: Passenger trains usually have priority over freight trains.
Crossing a border by rail can mean changing the locomotive.
Over short distances rail can lose its advantages.
questions.explanation: The passage says rail's share 'has hardly grown in many countries', which does not support rail overtaking road. The other three are stated: passenger trains usually take priority, border crossings can mean changes of locomotive, and over short distances transfer time can cancel rail's advantages.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Smart meters alone tend to bring only small savings.
wrong: Smart meters always cut household bills sharply.
Smart meters still need estimated bills.
Detailed readings reveal nothing about a household.
questions.explanation: Studies suggest the meters 'on their own lead to only small savings' without clear information or a suitable tariff. They end estimated bills, and detailed readings can reveal when people are at home.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Fewer people now live and work in the same village.
wrong: Professional crews have fully replaced volunteers in rural areas.
Volunteers have traditionally been recruited mainly among women.
Employers are now more willing to let staff leave work for call-outs.
questions.explanation: The fall in volunteers is linked to 'fewer people both live and work in the same village'. Professional crews cover only some of the gap, volunteers were recruited mainly among local men, and employers are less willing to let staff leave.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
questions.correct: Older workers train less, but short job-linked courses can reach them.
wrong: Older workers take part in training more often than younger ones.
Employers prefer to train staff who are about to retire.
Training for older workers works best in their own time.
questions.explanation: The passage reports less training among workers over fifty and describes what reaches them: short courses linked to their job, during working hours. It says the opposite of the other three statements.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Cheaper childcare has led to waiting lists in some places.
wrong: The number of childcare places has grown as fast as demand.
Providers say that funding is their main obstacle.
Price caps have reduced the number of parents taking up places.
questions.explanation: Early results show more parents taking up places 'but also waiting lists where the number of places has not grown at the same rate'. Providers name recruiting trained staff, not funding, as the main obstacle, and take-up has risen.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Heat pumps usually raise data centre heat before use.
wrong: Data centre heat is usually hot enough to use directly.
Most data centres already supply heat to district networks.
Reusing heat works best where no heating network exists.
questions.explanation: Because the heat is often at a low temperature, 'heat pumps are usually needed to raise it before use'. Only some operators pass on their heat, and the arrangement works best where a heating network already exists nearby.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: A box reused only a few times can be worse than single-use packaging.
wrong: Reusable boxes are lighter to produce than single-use packaging.
Return rates have been similar in every scheme.
Return rates are highest where few restaurants take part.
questions.explanation: A reusable box 'must make many trips before it has a smaller footprint' than single-use packaging, so with few uses it can be worse. Reusable boxes are heavier to produce, return rates varied widely, and they were higher where many restaurants in a small area took part.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Most plans keep traditional identity documents available.
wrong: Using a digital identity wallet will be compulsory.
A wallet always reveals the user's full identity.
Digital wallets can store only an identity document.
questions.explanation: 'Most plans therefore keep traditional documents available, and make the use of a wallet voluntary.' Users could share just one detail, and wallets can also store credentials such as a driving licence or a diploma.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: A paper bag used only once may do little for the environment.
wrong: Charges have rarely reduced the number of bags handed out.
Heavier plastic bags need less material to make than thin ones.
Every country charges for all kinds of carrier bag.
questions.explanation: Alternatives such as paper bags need more material, so 'their environmental benefit depends on being reused several times'. The number of bags usually fell sharply, heavier bags need more material, and only some countries charge for all carrier bags.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: A night mayor's role is usually advisory.
wrong: Night mayors can close venues that cause noise.
Residents' groups give priority to the interests of venues.
The night economy has always been treated as a source of jobs.
questions.explanation: 'The role is usually advisory.' Nothing is said about closing venues, residents' groups want sleep to carry at least as much weight as venues, and supporters say the night economy has long been treated only as a police problem.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Keeping seeds cold does not keep them usable forever.
wrong: Seed banks store only varieties that are widely grown today.
Stored seeds never need to be grown again.
Seed banks keep all their samples in a single country.
questions.explanation: Seeds 'slowly lose their ability to germinate', so samples must be tested and grown again. Banks protect varieties no longer widely grown, and some keep duplicates in other countries.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: People with fewer qualifications have used the accounts less.
wrong: Employers decide how the money in a learning account is spent.
Every training course offered has been of good quality.
All adults receive exactly the same credit in every scheme.
questions.explanation: The accounts are used most by people with higher qualifications, 'while those with fewer qualifications use them less'. The idea is to give individuals control rather than employers, some courses have been of little value, and some schemes give a larger credit to people with lower qualifications.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the passage?
questions.correct: Dimming street lights has been shown to increase crime.
wrong: Light at night can disturb migrating birds.
Some authorities switch lights off on quiet roads.
Some residents feel less safe on dimmer streets.
questions.explanation: Studies of the effect on crime 'have so far given mixed results', so the passage does not support an increase. The other three are stated: light disturbs birds that migrate at night, some authorities switch lights off on quiet roads, and some residents feel dimmer streets are less safe.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Some hungry children do not qualify under income rules.
wrong: Free meals for all cost less than meals for low-income families only.
Every school already had suitable kitchens when the scheme began.
All studies agree that concentration improves.
questions.explanation: Meals for all reach children 'who are not eligible under income rules, but still go hungry'. Universal meals cost considerably more, not all schools had suitable kitchens, and results on concentration differ between studies.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
questions.correct: Battery and hydrogen trucks each suit different journeys.
wrong: Hydrogen trucks have already replaced diesel on long routes.
Battery trucks are best for long-distance haulage.
Hydrogen can already be produced cheaply without fossil fuels.
questions.explanation: Battery trucks suit regional deliveries, hydrogen may suit long distances, and 'most observers expect both technologies to be used, for different kinds of journeys'. Refuelling stations are still very few, battery weight and charging time are obstacles over long distances, and clean hydrogen is still expensive.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Many preprint servers warn that the work has not been reviewed.
wrong: Preprints are checked by other scientists before they appear.
Journals generally refuse papers that were first preprints.
The media have always reported preprints as unconfirmed.
questions.explanation: 'Many preprint servers now display a warning that the work has not been reviewed.' Preprints appear before peer review, journals generally still accept them, and some have been reported as if they were established results.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Many free-day visitors already go to museums regularly.
wrong: Most free-day visitors are visiting a museum for the first time.
Visitor numbers are lower on free days than on paid days.
Crowded free days make visits more enjoyable.
questions.explanation: Surveys suggest that 'a large share of free-day visitors are people who already visit museums regularly'. Visitor numbers are much higher on free days, not lower, most free-day visitors are not first-timers, and staff say crowding makes visits less enjoyable.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Hedgerows were removed to make fields suit larger machines.
wrong: New hedgerows give their full benefits within a year.
Farmers are paid to cut hedgerows more often.
questions.explanation: Hedgerows were removed 'to create bigger fields suited to modern machinery'. A new hedgerow takes several years to give its full benefits, farmers are paid to cut less often, and hedgerows help reduce soil erosion.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Closing a street to cars does not always reduce footfall.
wrong: All private vehicles, including residents', are banned.
Traffic on surrounding roads always falls.
Retailers have lost customers in every case.
questions.explanation: Results have been mixed, 'with some streets gaining footfall and others losing it'. Residents keep access, traffic on surrounding roads may increase, and not every street lost customers.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Some sellers state how much battery capacity remains.
wrong: Refurbished phones cost about the same as new ones.
Refurbished phones are sold without any warranty.
Buyers no longer worry about software updates.
questions.explanation: Some sellers 'state the battery's remaining capacity'. Refurbished phones cost considerably less, usually come with a warranty, and some buyers remain wary about software updates.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Fluent machine output can hide errors from a reviser.
wrong: Machine translation is used for all legal texts without revision.
Revising machine output is always faster than translating from scratch.
Every administration publishes machine translations for citizens.
questions.explanation: Errors 'can be fluent and therefore easy to overlook'. Legal texts still need full human translation or careful revision, revision can be faster only for routine texts, and some administrations keep machine translation away from published texts.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Lowering pressure at night can reduce water losses.
wrong: Replacing old pipes is cheap and causes little disruption.
Acoustic sensors are used to repair leaks automatically.
No regulator sets targets for reducing leakage.
questions.explanation: Companies 'reduce pressure in the network at night, when demand is low, to lower losses'. Replacing pipes is expensive and disruptive, sensors detect leaks rather than repair them, and some regulators set targets.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
questions.correct: Local ownership can build support, but projects face practical hurdles.
wrong: Community energy projects are run entirely by large utilities.
Local ownership makes residents more likely to oppose installations.
Connecting community projects to the grid is simple.
questions.explanation: The passage says local ownership increases acceptance but that projects struggle with volunteers, grid connection and raising capital. Projects are owned by residents, ownership reduces opposition, and grid connection is described as complex.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Twinning activity has fallen partly for lack of younger volunteers.
wrong: Twinning partnerships began in the twenty-first century.
Twinning involves only official visits by mayors.
No association has managed to revive its partnership.
questions.explanation: Activity declined 'as the volunteers who ran the exchanges have grown older and fewer young people have taken over'. Twinning began in the mid-twentieth century, involves schools, clubs and cultural groups, and some associations have revived their partnerships.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the passage?
questions.correct: Phone bans have clearly improved pupils' results.
wrong: Some schools keep pupils' phones in lockers or pouches.
Some parents worry about contacting their children.
Many schools allow phones in particular lessons.
questions.explanation: Evidence on results 'is so far limited and mixed', so a clear improvement is not supported. The other three are stated: lockers or pouches, parents' concern about contacting children, and phones allowed in particular lessons.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Many older bridges were not designed for today's heavy lorries.
wrong: Inspection budgets have grown faster than the number of old bridges.
A weak bridge is always closed immediately.
questions.explanation: Many bridges 'were not designed for today's traffic, especially the number and weight of heavy lorries'. Budgets have not always kept pace, authorities may first lower weight limits or close a lane, and sensors monitor bridges between inspections.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Voluntary participation limits what these bodies can do.
wrong: All traders must take part in dispute resolution.
Most consumers already know these bodies exist.
Cases usually take longer than they would in court.
questions.explanation: Participation is voluntary in many sectors, 'which limits the reach of these bodies'. Consumers are often unaware of them, and where traders take part most cases are settled faster than in court.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Green roofs can reduce the risk of drains overflowing.
wrong: Green roofs make the building below warmer in summer.
Any existing roof can take a green roof without changes.
No city requires green roofs on new buildings.
questions.explanation: Green roofs hold back rainwater, 'which reduces the risk of drains overflowing'. They can lower the temperature below in summer, need a structure strong enough for the extra weight, and some cities require them on large new flat-roofed buildings.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Fish have often returned upstream after a barrier was removed.
wrong: Old dams are protected as heritage wherever they stand.
Old dams help sediment to move further downstream.
Removing a barrier never needs an assessment of local views.
questions.explanation: Monitoring after removal 'has often recorded fish returning upstream within a few years'. Only some structures are protected as heritage, dams trap sediment, and each case requires an assessment.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Café toilet schemes may not help at night.
wrong: The number of public toilets has risen in most towns.
Café toilet schemes cost more than public facilities.
Only tourists are affected by the lack of public toilets.
questions.explanation: In these schemes the toilets 'are available only during the businesses' opening hours', so they may be closed at night. Public toilets have fallen in number, the schemes cost less, and the passage names older people, parents and workers among those affected.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Some grants go to people who would have bought an e-bike anyway.
wrong: Grant recipients have stopped using their cars completely.
E-bikes are no help on hilly routes.
All schemes give the same grant to everyone.
questions.explanation: Some recipients 'would have bought an e-bike anyway, which means part of the grant money has no effect on behaviour'. Recipients replace the car for some trips, e-bikes make hilly routes manageable, and some schemes target particular groups.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Food banks need more cold storage for fresh products.
wrong: Surplus food donations are the same every day.
The food offered to charities is unsafe to eat.
Food banks have rejected the extra supply.
questions.explanation: Food banks 'need more refrigerated storage and transport to handle fresh products'. Donations vary from day to day, the food is still safe, and food banks have welcomed the extra supply.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
questions.correct: Applicants like adverts with salaries; pay gap effects are not yet known.
wrong: Salary rules have already closed pay gaps between men and women.
Employers' groups have fully supported publishing salaries.
Applicants prefer adverts that do not state a salary.
questions.explanation: Early studies suggest applicants 'respond positively to adverts that state a salary', but 'the effect on pay differences will take longer to measure', and employers' groups have raised concerns. The other statements contradict the passage.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Choosing sites carefully is seen as the most effective measure.
wrong: Turbines pose the same risk wherever they are built.
Painting a blade black has been tested at many sites.
Turbines are never stopped for passing birds.
questions.explanation: 'Careful choice of sites is therefore considered the most effective measure.' The risk varies greatly with location, black blades have been tested at only a few sites, and some operators stop turbines when birds approach.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Some parking apps charge an extra fee per payment.
wrong: Removing coins has raised the cost of collecting cash.
Every town has removed all cash-accepting machines.
Motorists' groups have welcomed the change.
questions.explanation: Motorists' groups say 'some apps charge an extra fee for each payment'. Councils say the change cuts collection costs, some towns kept cash machines, and motorists' groups have criticised the change.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the passage?
questions.correct: Most European homes now have air conditioning.
wrong: Air conditioning releases heat into the street outside.
External shading can reduce the need for cooling.
Heat pumps are generally more efficient than older units.
questions.explanation: The passage says air-conditioning use has increased, not that most homes have it. The other three are stated: heat released into the street, shading reducing the need for cooling, and heat pumps being more efficient than older units.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Some coworking spaces could not survive without public funding.
wrong: Village coworking spaces are always built as new buildings.
Remote workers rarely miss the company of colleagues.
All coworking spaces have kept going after funding ended.
questions.explanation: Some spaces 'have closed when it ended because too few people paid for regular use'. Many are in former schools, shops or stations, many remote workers miss company, and some closed after funding ended.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Some airports charge noisier aircraft more to land at night.
wrong: All airports ban night flights during certain hours.
Airlines and freight operators support night restrictions.
Night-time aircraft noise has no known link to health.
questions.explanation: Some airports 'use charges that make night landings more expensive for noisier aircraft'. Only several airports restrict night flights, airlines argue against restrictions, and night noise has been linked to health effects.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Some authorities have split large plots into smaller ones.
wrong: Waiting lists for allotments have disappeared.
Plot holders' associations support selling allotment land.
Allotments are owned by the people who grow on them.
questions.explanation: 'Some authorities have responded by dividing large plots into smaller ones.' Waiting lists can run to years, associations have opposed sales, and plots are rented, usually from authorities or associations.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Even trained staff can be fooled by a good phishing email.
wrong: Training removes the risk of phishing entirely.
Click rates usually rise after training.
questions.explanation: Experts warn that 'well-crafted messages can deceive even careful staff'. Training cannot remove the risk, click rates usually fall, and experts recommend combining training with two-step login.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
questions.correct: Stocks recover when advice is followed, but other factors also matter.
wrong: Fishing quotas have never helped a depleted fish stock recover.
Quotas are always set at exactly the level scientists recommend.
Rising sea temperatures have no effect on fish stocks.
questions.explanation: Stocks recovered where quotas followed scientific advice, recovery slowed where quotas were set higher, and factors such as sea temperature also matter. The other statements contradict the passage.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: It is unclear how far the scores change what people buy.
wrong: Repairability scores ignore the price of spare parts.
The scores have lowered the average repairability of products.
The score must be shown on every product sold.
questions.explanation: 'It is less clear how much the scores influence what consumers actually buy.' The score reflects the cost of spare parts, average scores of some products have risen, and it applies only to certain products.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Some programmes match retiring farmers with unrelated newcomers.
wrong: Most European farmers are under forty.
Newcomers to farming find land and capital easy to obtain.
Farms are always taken over by a family member.
questions.explanation: Some programmes 'match retiring farmers with new entrants who are not relatives'. A large share of farmers are over sixty, newcomers struggle to obtain land and capital, and many farms have no family member to take over.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: An open-plan office does not necessarily bring more face-to-face talk.
wrong: Open-plan offices always increase conversations between staff.
Staff rarely complain about noise in open-plan offices.
Quiet rooms have been removed from most offices.
questions.explanation: Several studies found face-to-face conversations 'can decrease after such a move'. Noise is the most common complaint, and some organisations now add quiet rooms.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the passage?
questions.correct: Artificial snow can be made at any temperature.
wrong: Artificial snow uses a lot of water and energy.
Some resorts are developing activities for summer.
questions.explanation: Artificial snow 'works only when temperatures are low enough', so it cannot be made at any temperature. The other three are stated: some resorts closed, artificial snow needs much water and energy, and some resorts develop activities for all seasons.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Reimbursement is usually capped at the cost of treatment at home.
wrong: Most patients now regularly seek treatment in another country.
Patients never have to pay upfront and wait for reimbursement.
Prior authorisation is never required for any treatment.
questions.explanation: 'Reimbursement is usually limited to what the treatment would have cost at home.' Relatively few patients use the option, the need to pay upfront is one of the reasons, and authorisation may be required for some treatments.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Recording frame numbers could help return stolen bicycles.
wrong: Most stolen bicycles are returned to their owners.
Theft has no effect on how much people cycle.
Secure parking now meets demand everywhere.
questions.explanation: Few stolen bicycles are returned 'partly because owners rarely record frame numbers', which is why registration schemes exist. Theft discourages cycling, and demand for secure parking often exceeds the spaces.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Some restaurant owners rely on income from bottled water.
wrong: Tap water is always of lower quality than bottled water.
Restaurants everywhere must serve free tap water.
Bottled water costs less than tap water.
questions.explanation: Some owners object that bottled water 'is a significant source of income'. Studies found tap water often of similar quality at a far lower cost, and the rule applies only in some countries.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Planting a tree does not guarantee that it survives.
wrong: Young trees need no watering once they are planted.
Large trees can be planted anywhere along a pavement.
Street trees raise the temperature of pavements in summer.
questions.explanation: Young trees need regular watering, and 'many die during their first dry summers'. Pipes and cables limit where large trees can grow, and trees lower pavement temperatures.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Driving specially to a locker can cancel its environmental benefit.
wrong: Parcel lockers always reduce emissions, however they are reached.
Lockers make failed deliveries more frequent.
Every city requires a separate locker for each delivery company.
questions.explanation: 'A special car trip can cancel out the benefit.' The benefit depends on how customers reach the lockers, lockers avoid failed deliveries, and some cities push for lockers shared by all companies.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Insect trends only become clear over many years.
wrong: Experts agree on exactly how much each cause has contributed.
Insect numbers are stable from one year to the next.
questions.explanation: Because numbers vary greatly with the weather, 'trends become clear only over many years'. The relative importance of the causes is debated, and some programmes rely on trained volunteers.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Some regions tax second homes more heavily.
wrong: Second-home owners never spend money in local businesses.
Owners' associations support higher taxes on second homes.
Villages with many second homes are busiest out of season.
questions.explanation: Some regions have responded 'with higher property taxes on second homes'. Owners bring spending during their stays, their associations oppose such measures, and villages can feel empty out of season.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: A recruited nurse may not start at full level straight away.
wrong: Guidelines encourage recruiting from countries with severe shortages.
Recruited nurses never need language training.
Health services have stopped training nurses at home.
questions.explanation: Recruited nurses often need language training and recognition of qualifications 'before they can work at their full level, which can take many months'. Guidelines discourage recruiting from countries with severe shortages, and services are trying to train more nurses at home.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
questions.correct: Energy certificates help compare buildings but may not show real energy use.
wrong: Energy ratings are the main factor in the price of a home.
Certificates always reflect the energy a building actually uses.
Energy certificates are optional when a building is sold.
questions.explanation: The certificates are meant to help compare running costs, but they 'may not reflect how much energy a building actually uses'. Location matters more for price, and a certificate must normally be provided.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Public charging generally costs more per unit than home charging.
wrong: Most charging takes place at fast chargers on motorways.
Worries about finding a charger no longer affect car buyers.
Chargers are never installed in residential streets.
questions.explanation: Public charging points 'are generally more expensive per unit of electricity'. Most charging happens at home or work, worries about chargers remain a reason to hesitate, and some chargers are built into lampposts in residential streets.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Most dietary salt comes from processed foods.
wrong: Salt is cut sharply in one step so consumers notice less.
Every producer has met the salt reduction targets.
Health organisations oppose rules on salt content.
questions.explanation: 'Most of the salt people eat comes not from the salt shaker but from processed foods.' Salt is reduced step by step, some producers missed the targets, and health organisations want rules if progress stalls.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Fees alone rarely pay for maintaining and replacing items.
wrong: Libraries of things lend only books and magazines.
Camping gear is the most borrowed type of item.
Items lent out never break or need replacing.
questions.explanation: Upkeep and replacement 'are ongoing costs that fees rarely cover in full'. The libraries lend household items, tools for repairs and gardening are the most popular, and broken items do need replacing.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the passage?
questions.correct: Temporary users usually become long-term tenants.
wrong: Some towns let artists use empty shops at low rent.
Some owners prefer to wait for a full-rent tenant.
questions.explanation: The passage describes temporary use 'until a long-term tenant is found' and does not say temporary users become that tenant. The other three are stated in the passage.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Crops eaten raw need the strictest water standards.
wrong: Reusing wastewater lowers the cost of irrigation.
Treated wastewater needs no further treatment for farms.
Public acceptance falls when people learn how water is treated.
questions.explanation: Standards depend on the crop, 'with the strictest standards for crops eaten raw'. Reuse needs additional treatment and pipes, which increase costs, and acceptance grows with understanding.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: An ombudsman can recommend but not overturn decisions.
wrong: Complainants must pay a fee to use an ombudsman.
Complaints should go to the ombudsman before the authority.
questions.explanation: An ombudsman 'cannot overturn a decision in the way a court can, but can recommend' action. The service is free, complainants usually raise the issue with the authority first, and ombudsmen publish their findings.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Making collection more convenient may raise participation.
wrong: Collected food waste can be used only for compost.
Participation is the same in every household.
Smells are not a problem in summer.
questions.explanation: Authorities that provide free liners and collect frequently 'tend to report higher participation'. Waste can also become biogas, participation varies, and smells put some households off, especially in summer.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Mentoring works better when mentors have time set aside for it.
wrong: Few new teachers leave in their first years.
Mentors are always chosen from other subjects.
New teachers always have a full timetable in their first year.
questions.explanation: Mentoring is linked to higher retention 'particularly when mentors teach the same subject and have time set aside for the role'. A significant share of new teachers leave early, and some schools give a lighter timetable.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the passage?
questions.correct: Green bridges are the most common type of wildlife crossing.
wrong: Cameras have recorded deer using wildlife crossings.
Fences can guide animals towards crossings.
Collisions with wildlife can endanger drivers.
questions.explanation: Green bridges are expensive, 'so tunnels and adapted culverts are more common'. The other three are stated: cameras recorded deer, fences guide animals, and collisions endanger drivers.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Remote interpreting suits some situations better than others.
wrong: There are more than enough qualified interpreters.
Deaf associations want remote interpreting to replace interpreters in person.
Remote interpreting is harder to arrange at short notice.
questions.explanation: Remote interpreting 'is not suitable for every situation', for example when a person is unwell. Interpreters are scarce, associations welcome it as an addition, and it has made interpreters easier to reach at short notice.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Travellers the gates cannot match are sent to a border guard.
wrong: Families with young children usually use the automated gates.
Automated gates are slower than manual checks.
No rules govern how the images may be stored.
questions.explanation: When the gates fail to match a traveller, 'the traveller is referred to a border guard'. Families with young children are usually sent to staffed desks, the gates are faster, and data protection rules govern storage.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Employers recognise micro-credentials to different degrees.
wrong: Micro-credentials require enrolling in a full degree.
Micro-credentials are already described in one standard format.
questions.explanation: Recognition varies 'partly because the quality and content of courses differ widely'. Micro-credentials avoid a full degree, and initiatives are only now working towards a standard description.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
questions.correct: Trams have returned in many cities, while some choose cheaper buses.
wrong: No European city has built a tram line since the 1980s.
Building tram lines is cheap and causes little disruption.
Buses can carry more passengers than trams.
questions.explanation: Many cities have built new tram lines since the 1980s, while some smaller cities chose high-quality buses at lower cost. Construction is costly and disruptive, and trams carry more passengers than buses.

questions.subject: Verbal reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.correct: Using the same method each year helps track population changes.
wrong: Organisers claim volunteers never misidentify a species.
Only trained scientists take part in the count.
The count changes its method every year.
questions.explanation: 'Because the same method is used each year, the results help scientists to track changes.' Organisers acknowledge misidentification, hundreds of thousands of members of the public take part, and the method stays the same.
